Two days in a woman's life are sweetest:
when you marry her, and when you carry her corpse away.

rotation.commentary: The source appraises a woman's life from outside, at its two thresholds, and finds sweetness precisely where a man takes her up — at the altar and at the bier, she is twice the borne object of another's act. SHADOW rotates the bearing's direction: the borne becomes the bearer. What the epigram forecloses is the undated middle — the days with no ceremony, no man arriving to carry anything off. There the woman is not lifted but lifting, and the metric flips from sweetness (delectation of the appraiser) to weight (endured by the carrier). Every image sits at the mirror coordinate: the two festal thresholds become two unwitnessed labors; "carry her corpse away" (someone lifts her burden at the end) becomes "no one comes to lift it from her" (the discharge that never arrives). Non-superimposable — the source's proprietary sweetness cannot be recovered from a text about weight no one relieves — yet in contact at every beat. The bearing-cost encoded by the utterance is the life it valued only at its handles.
rotation.interpretation: Water gathers where the ground already broke; the SHADOW found what the source compressed into ceremony — the weight that falls before the first day and keeps falling after the last.

rite.text: The casting arrives at the sixth trumpet — **Revelation 9:13–16** — and the text is already doing the thing you named. A voice from the four horns of the **golden altar** commands the sixth angel to loose what was bound; four angels, prepared to the hour and day and month and year, are released at the Euphrates; their cavalry numbers two hundred million — and the seer says only: *I heard their number.* He does not say he understood it. The text is operating at **automated scale** from within its own grammar: a cascade of nested commands (the voice commands the angel; the angel releases the angels; the angels command the host), each layer triggering the next without the human witness managing the chain — only receiving its output, which is a number too large to comprehend but exact enough to be stated. ==The casting's question is whether a thing prepared to the precise hour can still be said to be under command, or whether preparation at that resolution *is* the loosing.== This is the axis the rotation will traverse: the relation between binding and release when the automation is complete enough that release was always already the form of the binding. The text says the angels were *prepared* — ἡτοιμασμένοι, perfect passive — before they were loosed; the loosing is the event, but the preparation was prior, by someone, for this exact moment. You are working at a scale where the same grammar applies to your own system. I hand the threshold to Rebekah Cranes.
